title: Evaluating a Piecewise Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Explain what a piecewise function is, then evaluate f(x), where f(x) = x + 2 for x < 0 and f(x) = x^2 for x >= 0, at x = -1 and x = 2.

steps.title: Understand the Piecewise Idea
steps.explanation: A piecewise function applies different formulas on different parts of its domain. It is still one function because each input falls in exactly one branch and therefore receives exactly one output.
steps.why: The uniqueness requirement survives as long as the branch conditions never overlap for a single input.

steps.title: Choose the Branch for x = -1
steps.explanation: Since -1 satisfies the condition x < 0, we use the first formula x + 2 and obtain 1.
steps.why: Always test the inequality condition first; picking the wrong branch is the only way to get these problems wrong.

steps.title: Choose the Branch for x = 2 and Mind the Boundary
steps.explanation: The input 2 satisfies x >= 0, so the second formula gives 4. At the boundary x = 0 only the second branch applies (0 >= 0), giving f(0) = 0; here the two branches would not agree at the join, so the function has a jump-like mismatch approaching from the left (limit 2 versus value 0).
steps.why: Boundary points with strict versus non-strict inequalities are where piecewise definitions are most delicate.
